Contract status

FHGFF3 contract status
StatusReleased contract. schemaVersion "1.2" shipped in shared specification v0.6.0 on 2026-11-13.
Versions this schema accepts1.0, 1.1, 1.2. A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state any earlier minor of the same major, and holds each of them to that minor: what a later minor allows is invalid in an earlier one.
What it describesFHGFF3 is the FAIR-bioHeaders header for a GFF3 annotation file. It adds #~ YAML lines after the ##gff-version 3 line and one SHA-512/256 checksum over the file's exact bytes, and records which genome the coordinates refer to and how the annotation was made. Standalone JSON and YAML carry the same record.
What it does not coverFHGFF3 describes the annotation as a resource. It never makes the features valid: a header says nothing about whether a CDS is in frame or whether the terms are correct, and a GFF3 file without a header is still plain, valid GFF3. Feature and Sequence Ontology validation belongs to the gff3-validator, which reports header findings and feature findings separately.

Serializations with verified support

  • GFF3 with a #~ header block after ##gff-version 3 (optionally ##gff-version 3.x.y), before the first feature or ##FASTA line. Native directives such as ##sequence-region may sit among the header lines.
  • Standalone JSON and YAML metadata files.
  • No JSON-LD form and no HTML microdata form exists for FHGFF3 yet: keep the structured record as YAML when exporting a readable HTML table.

Tools that implement this contract

  • fair-bioheaders 0.10.0 (PyPI) bundles the v0.5.0 schema set and reads and writes FHGFF3 1.1, including extension fields, across combine, verify, validate, convert, strip, verify-links and assess. No toolkit release yet bundles the 1.2 schema, so a record that states 1.2 or uses a dotted lineage version is not validated by any released toolkit version while toolkit support for v0.6.0 is prepared.
  • gff3-validator validates GFF3 syntax, Sequence Ontology terms and biology, and reports FHGFF3 header checks (its HDR rules) alongside — never merged with — the feature results. Its header checks run through the toolkit it depends on, and its published 0.1.0 release pins an older fair-bioheaders, so a header citing v0.6.0 is reported as an unsupported schema version (HDR-007) rather than checked against FHGFF3 1.2 until that pin is widened. Feature validation does not depend on it.
  • The browser table builder on this site validates against its documented v0.4.0 snapshot (schemaVersion 1.0), not v0.6.0. Tracked in fair-bioheaders.github.io#15.

Schema location

  • Fixed schema URL of the current release: https://w3id.org/fair-bioheaders/fhgff3/v0.6.0. Cite the release a record targets: never hard-code a "latest" schema, and never check an unknown version against a different one.
  • The same bytes at the release tag: https://github.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/blob/v0.6.0/fhgff3.json, also fixed at commit 0ae18b00ee.
  • Development URL on main, the current contract, which moves: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/FAIR-bioHeaders/FAIR-bioHeaders-Specification/main/fhgff3.json.
  • Schema-version registry: schemas/versions.json and docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md.

Field reference

Every field of the contract appears here, including the fields and objects inherited from the shared core: nothing is left out because another type also uses it. Required means the key must be present; when present, requires lists the members that become mandatory once you supply an optional object. Constraints are reproduced verbatim from the schema, so a pattern you see here is the pattern the validator matches. Examples are the values stated by the released example records, which are synthetic, or an illustrative value where no example reaches the field.

Top-level fields

Every field of an FHGFF3 record. The record is a closed object: an unknown top-level key is invalid, with the single exception of the x- extension fields listed last.

Covers every byte of the GFF3 file — native directives, features and any ##FASTA section — except the root #~checksum: line (rules R1 to R4).

Sorting or tidying the GFF3 (for example gt gff3 -sort -tidy) changes bytes, so the copied header no longer verifies. Nothing repairs it.

1.2 came with shared release v0.6.0; 1.1 came with v0.5.0; 1.0 was first released in v0.4.0. Quote it in YAML.

A schema of version M.N also accepts records that state an earlier minor, and holds each of them to that minor: an x- extension field is invalid in a record that states 1.0 and valid in one that states 1.1 or 1.2, exactly as it would be invalid under the 1.0 schema (docs/SCHEMA-VERSIONS.md).

x-<name>Optionalany JSON valuesingle value or array, at any depth
  • pattern: ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$

Extension field (rule R15): a top-level key the standard does not define, holding any value the producer needs.

Valid from FHGFF3 1.1. Every other unknown key stays invalid, nested objects stay closed, and an x- key in a record that states 1.0 is rejected.

Extension fields are covered by the checksum and are omitted from JSON-LD and microdata writers (J9, M5, X9). FHGFF3 has no JSON-LD or microdata form at all today.

The gff3-validator reports header findings and feature findings separately; an extension key is a header finding, never a feature error.

Rules beyond a single field

FHGFF3 conditional and object-level rules, read from the schema bytes.
RuleWhat the contract requires
A genome link is requiredAt least one genome link is required: a genomeReference object, or a derivedFrom array holding an item with headerType: FHR and relationship: annotates. A record with neither is invalid — this is FHGFF3's central conditional rule.
At most one annotated genomeAt most one derivedFrom item may carry relationship: annotates, so a file cannot claim two annotated genomes.
annotates must name an FHR genomeAny derivedFrom item with relationship: annotates must state headerType: FHR: annotation of a transcriptome or protein set is not the genome link this contract requires.
Extension fields need the newer minorThe schema rejects extension fields in a record that states schemaVersion: '1.0', so a 1.0 record keeps exactly its 1.0 outcome. A record using an extension states 1.1 or a later minor.
No key may contain a line feedpropertyNames rejects any key containing a line feed, so a YAML continuation artefact cannot pass as part of a field name.
The record is a closed objectadditionalProperties: false — any other unknown top-level key is invalid, and every nested object is closed in the same way.
Extension fields (rule R15)Top-level keys matching ^x-[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_.-]*$ are accepted (rule R15, docs/FORMAT.md) from FHGFF3 1.1, released in shared specification v0.5.0.

What the schema cannot say

The contract is more than its JSON Schema. These requirements are normative for a conforming record, and a validator that cannot check them must say so:

  • The checksum covers every byte, including native directives, features and any ##FASTA section, except the root #~checksum: line. Sorting or tidying the file (gt gff3 -sort -tidy) invalidates a copied header.
  • annotation: "", taxon: {} and metadataAuthor: [] pass the released schema yet describe nothing; conforming values are non-empty.
  • featureCounts, soVersion, completeness and source[] are producer assertions. The schema checks shapes only: it does not know the Sequence Ontology and does not count features.
  • A header is not a genome match: verify-links compares recorded parent checksums or SeqCol digests against files on disk and reports matched, not matched or not checked.

It documents 63 fields: 25 at the top level and 38 inside 10 nested or reused objects. Regenerate and compare with python3 scripts/schema_fields.py --check, which the site checks run on every pull request. The specification repository stays the authority: this page is a rendering of it, not a second definition.
